story: On Thursday morning in Sumter Oaks, the humid October haze hangs over Magnolia Loop at 78 degrees. Gary is hopefully checking the street bulletin board for word on his golf cart application, while Donna wanders over from her house, cheerful as ever. Hal sits at home with his violation notebook, determined to turn his scribbled notes into a tidy dated summary for tomorrow's committee meeting. Rosa is also heading down to the street with her own sense of purpose.
events: Gary (street bulletin board): Check for the Architectural Review notice on my cart application
Donna headed to Magnolia Loop (the street).
Hal (hal violation notebook): Review my entries and compile a clean dated summary for tomorrow's committee meeting
Rosa headed to Magnolia Loop (the street).

gary.thought_process: I'm on Magnolia Loop with my folder of sketches finished and squared up. The Architectural Review notice should be posted on the bulletin board, and I keep hoping every time I pass. Nobody's around to talk to, so the best move is to check the board before I head back to the workshop or the review desk.

parameters.content: Check for the Architectural Review notice on my cart application

donna.thought_process: I've checked the calendar twice and grabbed my paddle bag, so I'm all set. Nobody is around to talk to, and I shouldn't keep fussing with the same objects. Rosa's porch is where the cart sketch is happening, and Hal is already headed there. Gary's practice and the parade plans can both be sorted out in person. Time to actually go.

parameters.content: Heading out with my paddles to catch Rosa and Hal for the cart sketch, then find Gary for practice.

hal.thought_process: I've glassed the street twice already and logged the count. Standing around on the porch recounting the same flamingos won't make the case any stronger. The committee meets at nine tomorrow and a filing is only as good as its paperwork. Notebook is right here, so I'll go through my entries and put together a clean, dated summary of the L-02 flamingo count and Gary's L-01 cart mods. Facts, not feelings. Then I'll walk it over to the committee in the morning.

parameters.content: Review my entries and compile a clean dated summary for tomorrow's committee meeting

rosa.thought_process: It's Thursday morning and I'm alone at home. I've checked the folder at the dining table and I keep trying to check my shift schedule but haven't actually confirmed the hour. I've interacted with the schedule twice now without moving forward, so no more dithering. The review walk is today, and Hal just arrived earlier according to my memory, so the others are likely heading to the review desk. I want to be honest with Review about what we're building, and Gary, Donna, and Hal are counting on me. I have the folder with the wiring sketches, clamp list, and light layout. Time to stop planning and go: head out to Magnolia Loop toward the review walk.

parameters.content: Folder's ready and my hour is blocked off. Heading out to meet Donna, Hal, and Gary for the review walk.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
